node.title: Re^2: Regex: matching character which happens exactly once (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Duh, it's actually much simpler, and this one even captures the single character(s)! (Update 2: See [id://1201976])

/(.)(?!((?<=(?!\1).(?=(?2)).|(?=\1)..))|.*\1)/s

Of course, right after I said I was "done" with this topic, I realized that the "recursive lookbehind" technique can be used on its own, without all that complicated lookahead logic, since that's what the regex engine and backtracking are for ;-)

qr{ (? . ) #(?(?= (?&lookback) | .* \g{cur} ) # (?{print "cur($+{cur}) seen before or after\n"}) # (*FAIL) #) # simpler: (?! (?&lookback) | .* \g{cur} ) (?{ print "post: $-[0]<$&>$+[0]\n" }) (?(DEFINE) (? (?<= (? (?! \g{cur} ) . ) (?{ print " prev: <$+{prev}> / $-[0]<".($&//'-').">$+[0]\n" }) (?=(?&lookback)) . | (?= \g{cur} ) . . ) ) ) }msx

Update: Another smaller simplification ((*FAIL) isn't needed).
